builder_plan.scenario: An agent looks good in demos, but you cannot tell which product tasks it fails.
builder_plan.change: Use the study's evaluation idea to inspect a small set of tasks with human-checked answers.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current evaluator and a manually reviewed reference set.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Agreement with human review, missed failures, false alarms, and evaluation cost per task.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: SeVerus: Context-Aware, Gamified Benchmarking for Rust Verification
summary: It replaces Verus benchmarks that hand agents the auxiliary lemmas by generating quests whose levels progressively remove proof context while a checker guards executable code, specifications, and proof soundness. Adoption costs Verus project selection, quest generation, independent checking, noisy binary-search evaluation, and rising agent API spend as context is withdrawn. It can fail as a production signal if the reader does not verify Rust code, if longer-quest failures are the real target, or if agents pass by alternative decompositions rather than recovering the withheld lemmas.
rationale: This is an evaluation methodology for Rust formal-verification agents rather than a deployable inference, training, or orchestration improvement for a constrained production stack.

claims.statement: It replaces Verus benchmarks that hand agents the auxiliary lemmas by generating quests whose levels progressively remove proof context while a checker guards executable code, specifications, and proof soundness. Adoption costs Verus project selection, quest generation, independent checking, noisy binary-search evaluation, and rising agent API spend as context is withdrawn. It can fail as a production signal if the reader does not verify Rust code, if longer-quest failures are the real target, or if agents pass by alternative decompositions rather than recovering the withheld lemmas.
The strongest evaluated agent solves the final level of 52 of 60 sampled quests but reliably solves only 35% of levels, with failures concentrated in longer quests.
